name: Sonia Garza
life: “I still remember the first train ticket I bought for a grown adult.” On Friday, near the approach to Seabright Court, Sonia likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I gave him my old bed. I asked the family to keep one night a week when I can stay too.
appearance: Sonia has a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape, a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, and a favorite piece of clothing, a brown corduroy jacket. It usually goes with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. When somebody else has the floor, Sonia presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Sonia has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To keep one regular family overnight visit.
family: George Crawford is Sonia’s half-sibling. Sonia is free to hang up first. George makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A red mitten*, George says, “I photograph everything we find. In every frame there is a different hand reaching into the corner.”
connections: Charlie Starr. Preparing a bedroom competes with the guest's own need for occasional space in the house.

reactions.situation: The returning father wants a family photograph immediately
reactions.response: Sonia asks each household member privately whether they want to be in the picture.
